name: Street Views and Mood in Guangzhou: Six Pairwise Questions
description:
Method replication: participants compare pairs of street views from central Guangzhou on the paper's six mood questions (which place looks more motivated, happier, more likely to arouse positive-social emotion, more focused, more relaxed, more depressed), 6 pairs per question; the images are not the paper's stimuli (92 re-fetched Baidu street views of Yuexiu, Liwan, Haizhu and Tianhe, 2019–2022, square 90° views with the camera car cropped off).

Original study: Chen, Li, Luo, Xie, Yao, Wu & Xia (2022), Science of the Total Environment 816, 151605. On the online platform "Assessing the Effects of Street Views on Mood", 1,590 Guangzhou participants (mean age 24.5, about 70% female) compared pairs drawn from 2,996 Tencent street views (512 × 512, 90° field of view, 2018–2020), with one of the six questions asked at random for each pair: 101,458 comparisons in all. Strength-of-schedule scores trained machine-learning models that mapped mood states over 199,754 images of the four central districts.

Differences from the original study: (1) Baidu street views instead of the authors' Tencent images, which are not released; (2) the six questions come in blocks of 6 pairs each instead of a random question per pair, and each participant makes 36 choices (the paper averages about 64 per participant); (3) only sex and age are asked, as in the paper.
author: Chen, Li, Luo, Xie, Yao, Wu & Xia
